title: Patch: the AI's imagined opponent switches a spent attacker to Defense Position

**Issue #1696 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #1696: Patch: the AI's imagined opponent switches a spent attacker to Defense Position
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the practice AI weighs a move, it plays out the opponent's likely reply. That imagined opponent attacks sensibly but never repositions: a unit with nothing worth attacking stays in Attack Position, where a real defender would tuck it into Defense Position to shield the hero. The AI's own search already tries those switches for itself — only the reply model lacks them — so it slightly overvalues racing lines, expecting defenders to stay exposed. After this, the imagined reply also tries switching a unit with no good attack into Defense Position.

## Why

- `simulate_reply`'s fixed steps (`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`) include `deft_switch` (Def→Atk for Deft units that can then attack) and `ranked_attacks`, but no Atk→Def branch; the seat's own beam tries every switch (`crates/ai/src/candidates.rs`).
- Reply scoring is what ranks the AI's finalist lines (spec §9.9), so a defender who would hide a useless attacker is currently modeled as leaving it in Attack Position.

## Proposal

After the Deft step, for each unit `legal` lists a SwitchPosition for whose best attack value is at or below zero, try Atk→Def and keep it when the opponent's own `evaluate` prefers the result — the existing `best_try`/`reduce_for` pattern, bounded by the `AI_REPLY` counters.

## Where it lands

`crates/ai/src/reply.rs`, `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (any new bounds as named constants), `crates/ai/tests/ai/`. Spec §4.1, §9.9, R49, R964000.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A seeded reply where a unit has no positive attack and a switch is legal: it switches when `evaluate` prefers Defense Position and stays when it doesn't.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai` green; a dev-run or gate smoke shows no regression.
- [ ] New bounds are named constants.

## Size and risks

Small-medium. `evaluate` underpricing attack could cause over-switching — bounded attempts and the seeded test control it.
```
